content.text:
This structure is dabigatran, and I read it region by region.

- **Amidine end:** a benzene ring carries C(=N)N (amidine) at one para position and NH–CH2 at the other.
- **Benzimidazole:** the CH2 attaches to C2 of the benzimidazole. N1 carries a methyl group, and the other ring nitrogen (N3) is the =N.
- **Amide:** the benzene ring of the benzimidazole carries a C(=O) group that bonds to a tertiary nitrogen. That nitrogen bears a 2-pyridyl group and a CH2CH2COOH chain.

The ring fusion follows the drawing. N1 (with methyl) attaches to the ring carbon at the top (c3a-type) of the fused benzene, and N3 attaches to the lower fusion carbon. The carbonyl-bearing carbon is the right-hand vertex of the benzene ring. Going around that ring: the fusion carbon next to N1, then the top-left CH, the top-right CH, the carbonyl-bearing C, the bottom CH, and the fusion carbon next to N3. The carbonyl carbon is therefore para to the N1-side fusion carbon, which matches dabigatran.

SMILES: CN1C(CNc2ccc(C(N)=N)cc2)=Nc2cc(C(=O)N(CCC(=O)O)c3ccccn3)ccc21
